ca_reggie_dome.blurb: Reggie Dome is a compact granite dome in the Wonderland of Rocks section of Joshua Tree National Park, set among the rocks close to the Boy Scout trail parking area. It holds about two dozen climbs, mostly traditional with a handful of bolted lines, a top rope and a boulder problem. Grades run from easy fifth-class up to the low 5.11s, with the bulk in the 5.9 and 5.10 range and a good number of friendlier leads in the 5.5 to 5.8 band. Expect a blend of cracks and faces on solid rock. Most lines sit on the north and northeast sides, which stay shaded all day, while the west side catches afternoon sun, so it suits warmer days better than cold ones.

ca_turtle_rock_2.blurb: Turtle Rock is a bouldering formation on Ring Mountain, a hilltop open space in Tiburon in Marin County, a short hike beyond the better-known Split Rock. It has about two dozen problems on serpentine rock, nearly all of them easy to moderate, making it a good pick for beginners and intermediates; only a few reach V4 or V5. Expect a mix of short problems, taller ones and a long traverse, with sweeping views toward the Bay and the city skyline. Poison oak often grows at the base of the rock and is easy to miss in the tall grass, and the summit ridge can be windy, so bring layers.
ca_turtle_rock_2.parking_note: Leave the car in the turnaround at the top of steep Taylor Road in Tiburon, on the right side of the cul-de-sac.
ca_turtle_rock_2.approach: From the cul-de-sac, go on foot around the locked gate and up the paved road, then bear left onto dirt paths that cross the ridge. Turtle Rock comes into view below once you top out. It sits beyond and to the west of Split Rock.

ca_4_right_of_peapod.blurb: Right of Peapod is a stretch of a long volcanic rock band on Eagle Peak, high in Lassen Volcanic National Park at roughly 8,700 feet. About two dozen single-pitch routes are here, mostly traditional with a few bolted lines and top ropes. The difficulty ranges from easy fourth and fifth class to the low 5.12s, with the largest group around 5.10 and a fair number of moderate lines for newer leaders. Most parties gravitate to this side of the Peapod formation, while the far left end sees few visitors. The elevation keeps it cooler than the lowlands, which makes it a summer escape, and the walk in is uphill.

ca_supreme_wizard_formation.blurb: Supreme Wizard Formation is a sport wall on the gorge's eastern side in the Owens River Gorge near Bishop, beyond Monkey to Monkey Cliff, and marked by a large roof. Around two dozen routes are here, nearly all bolted single pitches, and one trad line. Grades start at 5.8 and climb to the low 5.13s, with most between 5.10 and 5.12, so it leans toward intermediate and strong climbers rather than beginners. Expect steep, powerful climbing, with several well-liked moderates for warming up. The gorge floor sits around 5,600 feet in the Eastern Sierra.
ca_supreme_wizard_formation.approach: Walk in from the upper gorge by way of the Lower Elbow Room area, or arrive from the central gorge side.

ca_mecca.blurb: Mecca is a steep sport-climbing section of Lower Cathedral Rock in Yosemite Valley, well known for hard face climbing on granite. Of its roughly two dozen routes, most are bolted, with a few trad lines and one aid route. Grades concentrate heavily in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with a handful of 5.10 and 5.13 routes and very little below that, so it is not a place for beginners. The wall faces north, staying shady in summer and cold in winter, with only brief morning sun in high season, which makes it a good refuge from valley heat.

ca_main_wall_the.blurb: The Main Wall is the largest and busiest section of Grizzly Dome, a granite crag in the Feather River canyon beside Highway 70 in the Lost Sierra. Roughly two dozen routes here are mostly bolted single pitches, with a few trad lines, including some multi-pitch ones, and a couple of top ropes. Grades run from 5.7 to the low 5.12s, centered on 5.9 and 5.10, so it suits a mix of abilities. The wall faces southwest and the approach is only a few steps from the parking lot. Many first bolts are high, so bring a stick clip. Weather is often pleasant, and the lot frequently fills.
ca_main_wall_the.approach: The base of the wall is right beside the parking lot, only a few steps away. Some routes can be belayed from your car.
